source.vendored: daisyui-5.7.32/theme/*.css and themeOrder.js, copied byte-for-byte out of that tarball. The suite parses them; no theme value or theme name is transcribed into this file.
source.meanings_from: daisyui.com/docs/colors/ (the 'Where to use' column) and daisyui.com/theme-generator/ (the eight non-colour controls)
source.note: `published` is a quotation. Nothing here may edit it; a reading that disagrees says so in `maps_to`/`stance`/`why`. The suite pins a hash over the vendored bytes and over the quoted column, so a reworded quotation is a failing run rather than a silent one.

reading.published: base surface color of page, used for blank backgrounds
reading.why: the page ground under another word: `#Design.shell.bg` already resolves to `neutral`. The reading is a rename, and the value carries verbatim — press's own inks are `hsl()`, so the bucket was never hex-shaped.

reading.published: base color, darker shade, to create elevations
reading.why: press's `surface` is the raised card and is LIGHTER than `neutral`; daisyUI's base-200 is a step DARKER than base-100. A second surface has a name; the elevation direction does not.

reading.published: base color, even more darker shade, to create elevations
reading.why: pronto's third surface is a muted fill, not a third elevation rung. Nothing orders `surface` against `surface-muted`, so a theme cannot say which is the further step.

reading.published: Foreground content color to use on base color
reading.why: press's `primary` IS the ink and `#Design.shell.fg` resolves to it, so the role lands — but the name says brand where daisyUI says foreground-on-base, and a theme wanting ink and a brand hue has one slot for two.

reading.published: primary brand color, The main color of your brand
reading.why: `accent` is press's only brand hue. daisyUI publishes three — primary, secondary, accent — so the first fits and the other two have nowhere published to go.

reading.published: Foreground content color to use on primary color
reading.why: pronto publishes no on-colour role at all. `#Design.colors` admits one the moment someone writes it — cue accepts `{}` and the closed twin then demands a dark half, so the cost is two declarations rather than a refusal. The cost that bites is that the PRESET names none: every app would coin its own spelling, and a component set binds to a published name or to nothing. Concretely, a screen writing `background: var(--accent)` has no theme-safe foreground — it reads under press, whose accent is a dark green, and is unreadable under `acid`, whose accent is a near-white lime.

reading.published: secondary brand color, The optional, secondary color of your brand
reading.why: the second brand hue. press's `secondary` is muted grey INK (#6B7076), not a brand colour, and the one brand slot is already spent on daisyUI's primary. The name is not refused — it is TAKEN, and writing daisyUI's value into it rebinds press's ink silently, which is why `maps_to` may not be derived from a shared word.

reading.why: a published name with the opposite meaning: daisyUI's `neutral` is a dark unsaturated UI colour, press's `neutral` is the page ground. cue accepts the write and inverts the theme without complaint, which is the collision this reading exists to keep apart.

reading.published: Radius / Selectors — checkbox, toggle, badge
reading.why: a third radius role. `#Design.rounded` is an open map and takes `selector` with no twin at all, so this one costs a single line — but press does not publish it, `--r-full` is a 999px pill rather than a selector radius, and abyss, caramellatte, lofi, nord and silk set selector ABOVE box, which a sm/md/full ladder cannot state whatever it is called.

reading.published: Radius / Fields — button, input, select, tab
reading.why: press names radii by SIZE — sm/md/full — and daisyUI by ROLE. The value lands, but nothing in press says which elements read `--r-sm`, and in cupcake, forest, pastel and valentine `--radius-field` (2rem) EXCEEDS `--radius-box` (1rem), which an ordered ladder cannot state.

reading.published: Radius / Boxes — card, modal, alert
reading.why: the value lands on the larger of press's two named radii, but the binding is by size and not by element class, so a theme cannot move boxes without moving every other use of `--r-md`.

reading.published: Sizes / Selectors base size — checkbox, toggle, badge
reading.why: no published control geometry for checkboxes, toggles and badges: press's `control` bucket names field heights only. The bucket is open and takes the key untwinned, so this is a vocabulary gap and not a schema one.

reading.published: Sizes / Fields base size — button, input, select, tab
reading.why: daisyUI publishes ONE base unit and derives five field heights as `calc(var(--size-field) * N)`; press declares four independent heights. The unit has somewhere to land, but a theme that rescales every control with one number has no single press field to set.

reading.published: Border Width — All components
reading.why: `--border-size-1..5` publishes 1px and 2px as RUNGS, and a rung is not a switch: daisyUI's `--border` changes every component at once where press makes each stylesheet pick a rung. A role holding the switch is admitted by `#Design.control`; nothing publishes one. cupcake, pastel, caramellatte and silk set 2px.

reading.published: Depth Effect — 3D depth on fields & selectors
reading.why: elevation is answered differently on purpose. daisyUI multiplies a scalar into `color-mix()`es taken off the component's own background; this design publishes the Open Props `--shadow-1..6` ladder over seven twinned inks. `#Design.control` would take the scalar — the probe shows it — so this is a refusal and not a hole.

reading.published: Noise Effect — Noise pattern on fields & selectors
reading.why: a texture layer is a background-image RULE carrying an SVG data-URI. `#Design.control` would hold the scalar, but nothing in the design layer emits a rule, so carrying the number would publish a switch no stylesheet could read.

pronto_only.why: a border COLOUR. daisyUI tokenizes no border colour at all — every component derives one with `color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-base-content) 20%, #0000)` or reaches for base-200.
muted grey ink. daisyUI's `secondary` is a brand hue, so the word matches and the meaning does not; binding them would put a brand colour where press puts a caption.
pronto's elevation answer: seven pre-composed inks carrying the appearance half of `--shadow-1..6`. daisyUI's answer is the scalar `--depth`.
daisyUI derives every control height from `--size-field` rather than naming any, so its contract has no counterpart for a named height.
a control's inset. daisyUI derives padding per component from `--size-field` and `--border`.
daisyUI tokenizes no motion: no duration, no easing, no displacement.
a 999px pill. In daisyUI a pill is Tailwind's `rounded-full` utility, outside the theme contract entirely.
the terminal's own chrome, pointing at a role. No theme contract reaches the shell.
daisyUI publishes NO spacing scale; it defers to Tailwind's `--spacing`. The whole `--sp-*` role set is outside its contract.
a named type purpose. daisyUI's themes tokenize no type at all — sizes and leadings are Tailwind's utilities, outside the theme — so no published token reaches press's typescale.
